idea-plugin.name: Fancy Event Sounds
idea-plugin.description:
Give your IDE a voice 🔊

Fancy Event Sounds plays a sound when something happens in your IDE, so you get feedback without having to watch the Run window. You hit Run, look away at your browser or a second monitor, and your ears tell you what happened.

What it does

  • Run started — a sound the moment a run or debug configuration launches.
  • Run failed to start — instant feedback when a configuration cannot launch, instead of silently staring at an empty console.
  • Per-event toggles — turn on only the events you actually care about.
  • Your own sounds — point any event at a custom .mp3 file.
  • Never blocks the IDE — audio plays on a background thread, and a new event stops the previous sound so notifications never pile up.

Configuration

Everything lives under Settings/Preferences → Tools → Event Sounds. Toggle each event, and optionally browse for a custom .mp3. Leave a path empty to use the bundled sound. If a custom file goes missing, the plugin falls back to the bundled sound rather than failing.

Settings are stored application-wide, so they apply to every project in the IDE.

Why this plugin exists

Plugins that did this used to exist, but they stopped being maintained and broke on modern IDEs. This is a maintained fork, rebuilt against a current IntelliJ Platform and actively developed. It continues the work of Event Sounds, which itself continued the original.

Source, roadmap and issue tracker: github.com/mordisk10/event-sounds. Feature requests for new events are welcome.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.0.1

  • Added a settings screen under Tools → Event Sounds.
  • Each event can now be enabled or disabled independently.
  • Custom .mp3 files can be selected per event, with an automatic fallback to the bundled sound when a file is missing.
  • Rebuilt against the 2023.2 platform (build 232 and newer).

1.0.0

  • First release: sounds for run configurations that start and that fail to start.
